history.body: Hi, I came across the Pearl Residences ad. We’re looking to upgrade from our rental sometime this year. What’s the project like?

Pearl Residences is a freehold residential condominium in Seberang Jaya. Phase 1 homes are 900 sq. ft. with 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony, and the maintenance fee is RM0.18 per sq. ft. including sinking fund. One important timing point: completion is expected in Q4 2029, so it wouldn’t be ready for a move this year. How fixed is your timing for the upgrade?
We don’t need to move this year; we’re hoping to buy within the next year if we find the right place. So we’d be planning ahead for the Q4 2029 completion.

That makes the timing more workable—you can plan ahead for the expected Q4 2029 completion rather than needing an immediate move. Since you’re looking to upgrade from renting, a viewing would let you judge whether the 900 sq. ft., 3-bedroom layout feels right for your day-to-day needs. Would you like to arrange a viewing?

Q4 2029 still feels quite far, and we’re not in a rush to move. Our rental feels small with our little one, so I’d want to understand whether the layout would give us more usable space before planning a visit.

That’s fair—the expected Q4 2029 completion is a longer wait, so it makes sense to first see whether the space could work for your family. Type A is 900 sq. ft., with an open-plan living, dining and kitchen area, no long internal corridor, and a small storage area. Those features can help use the floor area efficiently, though I can’t say it will feel bigger than your rental without comparing the layouts. A viewing would let you judge the room proportions and how the living area might work for your family. There’s no need to rush; if that sounds useful, I can help arrange one.
That could help, especially if the third room gives us somewhere to keep our little one’s things. I’d like to review the approved plan with my partner first, though, before arranging a visit.

That makes sense—reviewing the approved plan with your partner first should help you judge whether the third room could work for your little one’s things. The details we have are conceptual, so I can’t confirm the room’s exact usable space without the approved plan. I’ll check whether we can share it with you; after you’ve reviewed it, we can see whether a visit would be useful.
